tone.target: bright 60s British pop-rock crunch with jangly open chords
tone.profile: bright 60s British pop-rock crunch with jangly open chords
tone.summary: A clean signal chain utilizing the AC30 TB and UK Vintage 4x12 for classic British pop-rock crunch, enhanced by Chorus and Room reverb for vintage depth.

rig.name: Cream - I Feel Free - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide a subtle, bright edge-of-breakup and slight chime without heavy grit.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used for its clean boost character rather than aggressive overdrive.

alternatives.reason: Slightly more robust, but Green OD better matches the 'chime' requirement.

blocks.purpose: Bypass to keep the signal clean and focused on natural amp breakup.
blocks.gap: The target tone requires minimal gain structure; a dedicated distortion unit is unnecessary.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the bright, chimey sound of a Vox AC30, essential for 60s pop-rock.
Provide the classic British cabinet sound and bright voicing.
Brighten the high end and tighten up the low-mids for jangly chords.
blocks.gap: Used to fine-tune the bright, open chord voicing required by the 'jangly' description.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle width and vintage movement without sounding modern or distracting.
blocks.gap: Chorus is used sparingly to add depth, avoiding the overly wet sound of other modulations.

blocks.purpose: Provide a dryish vintage room ambience without the wash of modern reverb.
blocks.gap: The 'dryish vintage room' clue points directly to this module.

alternatives.reason: Too bright and artificial for a 60s pop-rock sound.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the current IR for one that better captures the open, bright sound of a vintage British combo.

proposals.reason: The current 4x12 might be too large/boxy for the desired jangly, chimey pop sound.
